title: Priority Admission Operator: coordinated load-shedding and graceful degradation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem:
Redwood must keep inference endpoints within SLOs during overload, multi-region failover, and partial infra degradation. Current ad-hoc shedding (basic tenant throttles and global rate limits) doesn't coordinate across regions or gracefully reduce quality. We need a single operator (Priority Admission Operator, PAO) that enforces prioritized admission, coordinates circuit-breaker triggers, and applies graduated degradation modes (soft-degrade) per-tenant and per-route while preserving core availability for critical workloads.

Goals:
- Implement a runtime operator that admits requests according to configurable priority lanes (system, paid-critical, paid-standard, best-effort).
- Support admission control knobs: token-bucket quotas, dynamic weighted drop probabilities, and per-tenant burst handling.
- Provide graceful degradation modes: max-token truncation, aggressive KV-prefix cache reuse, deterministic model-size fallback (e.g., 70B -> 13B), and compressed responses for embeddings/structured outputs.
- Ensure multi-region coordination so failovers don't amplify load (global admission hints and per-region backpressure signals).
- Expose observability and control: per-priority metrics, SLO burn-rate alerts, and an emergency global circuit-breaker switch.

Non-goals:
- Replacing full global sharding; this ticket focuses on admission and degradation logic and APIs only.
acceptance_criteria: PAO implemented in runtime as a pluggable admission layer and enabled behind a runtime flag
Four priority lanes configurable per-tenant with token-bucket parameters and burst windows
Degradation policies (token truncation, model fallback, KV reuse, compression) selectable per-lane and runtime-overrideable
Per-region backpressure API that broadcasts summarized admission state to other regions within 2s of change
End-to-end tests demonstrating preservation of P99 latency and error-rate SLOs for high-priority lane under synthetic spike
Dashboard panels added to Console showing admission decisions, drop rates, and SLO burn by tenant and region
Runbook and gradual rollout plan documented and dry-ran in staging with chaos injection
discussion: 2025-02-12 [Ava Martinez]: Kickoff notes — proposed PAO concept, priority lanes, and candidate degradation modes. Linked design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/PAO+Design
2025-02-14 [Rohit Patel]: Prototype admission API implemented in runtime branch 'pao/prototype'. Initial token-bucket and drop-probability hooks are plumbed into RequestRouter.

2025-02-16 [Sofia Chen]: Raised concern about model-fallback fidelity. Suggested adding deterministic quality estimation per-prompt to avoid silent quality regressions; will add evaluation harness to Optimize pipeline.
2025-02-19 [Priya Nair]: Multi-region coordination note — recommend a gossip-lite protocol for region hints (heartbeat + summarized load) rather than full global consensus to reduce complexity.

2025-02-21 [Security]: Flagged compression of structured outputs may expose PHI in logs if misconfigured. Added security_review_required = true and KMS/HSM audit requirement for related config endpoints.

2025-02-24 [Rohit Patel]: Integration test results in staging: under 3x baseline QPS spike, high-priority lane maintained P99 latency, best-effort drop rate reached 73% as expected. Attached perf report: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/paotest
decisions: Adopt four default priority lanes: system, critical-paid, standard-paid, best-effort (configurable per-customer)
Use token-bucket for steady-state limits combined with probabilistic early-drop when backlog grows (weighted by tenant priority)
Implement model-size fallback as a ranked list (eg. model-v2-70B -> model-v1-13B -> model-quantized) with quality-estimation tags in catalog
Multi-region coordination will use a push-based 'region-hint' channel with 2s target propagation for emergency backpressure
Expose a global 'panic' circuit-breaker that can be toggled by SRE/Console for emergency shedding overrides
